publication_redaction.note: F2 is disclosure-flagged at urgency 'prompt': the authors and the journal must be notified before this record leaves the registry, and pii_description must be coarsened first. Do not publish any worked example that demonstrates the re-identification route. package_locus on every finding needs a read-through before release: a deposit path can name a participant.

bibliographic.title: Self-talk training and endurance performance in competitive cyclists: a randomised controlled trial

design.notes: Two arms (self-talk training vs attention-matched control), three measurement waves over eight weeks.

sample.population_description: Competitive amateur road cyclists, 19-41, recruited through three regional clubs.

reported_statistics.main_result_description: Self-talk training improved 20-km time-trial performance relative to control at wave 3.
reported_statistics.power_analysis_description: A priori G*Power analysis targeting 80% power for d = 0.65 gives a required n of 78.4, reported in the paper as 78. Rounded DOWN: the requirement is 79. The achieved analytic n of 78 therefore meets the printed target and misses the real one by one participant.

package.data_completeness_note: Wave-2 accelerometer data referenced in Section 2.4 are not deposited; the derived summary is.
package.runs_as_shipped_note: 00_master.R runs after repointing two absolute paths; 04_bayes.R aborts because the brms version it needs is not pinned anywhere in the deposit.
package.das_text: All data and analysis code supporting the findings of this study are openly available on the Open Science Framework.
package.das_mismatch_description: The statement says all data are available; the wave-2 accelerometer series underlying Section 2.4 and Figure 3 is not in the deposit, only its derived per-participant summary.

governance.coi_text: The authors declare no competing interests.
funders: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science
governance.ethics_body: University ethics committee (named in the paper)
governance.consent_evidence: The paper states written informed consent was obtained; neither the paper nor the deposit says whether it covered open republication of participant-level data.
governance.pii_description: One deposited file pairs a participant code with a session date; the pairing narrows most participants to a single club training slot. Reported to the authors at the coarsest level that lets them find it; the file and column names are in the disclosure email, not in this record.
governance.pii_detector_scope: Scanned all 213 files under pkg/. Forms covered: bare P-codes, underscore-prefixed codes (CYC_P07), and club-prefixed codes; dates in ISO, dd/mm/yyyy and dd.mm.yyyy; clocks hh:mm:ss. Two xlsx workbooks and one rds were decoded before scanning rather than pattern-matched as bytes. Negative control: ordinary prose from the paper's Methods does not fire. Positive controls used out-of-range ids (P999).

disclosure.statement: One deposited file pairs a participant code with the date of that participant's testing session. Combined with the club training schedules published on the three clubs' own websites, the pairing narrows most participants to a single slot. Re-identification requires that auxiliary information, so the exposure is real but not immediate.
disclosure.consistent_with: correction (deposit modification); the repository supports a direct file modification request, so no new deposit is required

assertions_withheld.note: This programme reports only what the artifacts show. It makes no finding as to cause, intent, or good faith, and recommends no editorial action. 'consistent_with' fields locate findings against published editorial standards and are descriptive only.

findings.claim: The deposited data and code return a standardised effect of 0.58 for the time-trial result; the article reports 0.65.

evidence.operation: execute as supplied, unmodified, R 4.4.1; effsize 0.9.0
evidence.tolerance_note: Reproduced identically under effsize 0.8.1 and 0.9.0 and under all four exclusion rules the article describes. The gap is not attributable to environment, seed or solver version.

findings.remedy_description: Correct d and its interval in Table 2 and the abstract; the direction and significance of the result are unchanged.
benign_explanations_ruled_out: Different exclusion set: reproduced under all four exclusion rules described in the paper; none gives 0.65.
Rounding: 0.58 does not round to 0.65 under any convention.
Package version drift: reproduced under effsize 0.8.1 and 0.9.0 with identical results.

verifiers.method: re-ran work/f1_effect_size.R on a clean checkout
recomputed d by hand from the deposited group means and SDs
verifiers.notes: 0.582 by hand; matches to the printed precision.

findings.claim: A deposited file pairs each participant's code with the date of their testing session.

evidence.artifact: pkg/data/ (one file; named in the disclosure email, not here)
evidence.operation: scan every deposited file for a participant code and a date on one row
evidence.expected: no participant code beside a date
evidence.observed: one file pairs both across all rows

findings.consistent_with: correction (deposit metadata); removal is not in question
findings.remedy_description: Drop the date column, or coarsen it to study week, and request a direct file modification through the repository -- OSF supports this without a new deposit.
benign_explanations_ruled_out: Dates could be audit-run artefacts rather than testing times: excluded, they match the wave schedule in Table 1.
Codes could be non-unique: excluded, each code appears in exactly one row per wave.

findings.claim: The shipped script assigns the attention-matched task to both arms in wave 1; the Methods describe two distinct conditions from wave 1 onward.

evidence.operation: trace the condition variable from allocation through the wave-1 model call
evidence.expected: two distinct conditions at wave 1, per Methods section 2.3
evidence.observed: both arms receive the attention-matched task at wave 1; the condition column is constant within that wave

findings.consistent_with: retraction, or retraction with republication where a valid analysis survives in the same materials
findings.remedy_description: Re-run the wave-1 comparison with the arms as described, or amend the Methods to describe what was run. Either way Table 2 and the abstract need revisiting.
findings.changes_conclusion_which: The claim that the wave-1 difference establishes an early training effect; as shipped, the wave-1 contrast is between two identical conditions.
benign_explanations_ruled_out: A deliberate wash-in design: excluded, the paper describes no wash-in and the preregistration specifies distinct arms from wave 1.
A superseded script left in the deposit: excluded, 00_master.R sources this file and no alternative exists in the package.

verifiers.method: re-ran work/f3_arm_assignment.R and independently traced the condition column
verifiers.notes: Confirms both arms share the wave-1 task, but the constancy holds for 79 of 82 rows, not all 82; three rows carry a distinct code that the model call drops. The finding stands; the claim was narrowed to match.

findings.claim: Forty-one statistical tests are performed in the analysis code and twelve are reported, with no correction for multiplicity.

evidence.operation: inventory every call to a test function, hand-classify each as a hypothesis test or a diagnostic, then re-run the reported set under Holm correction over the 29 hypothesis tests
evidence.observed: seven of the twelve reported results lose significance under Holm over the full family of 29
evidence.tolerance_note: Which tests constitute the family is a judgement and is contestable; the alternative used is stated so it can be disagreed with.

findings.remedy_description: Report the full test family, or state the confirmatory subset preregistered in advance and correct the exploratory remainder.
benign_explanations_ruled_out: Unreported tests could be diagnostics rather than hypothesis tests: excluded by hand-classifying all 41 calls; 29 are hypothesis tests on outcome variables.
The preregistration could designate the twelve: excluded, it names seven.

findings.claim: The wave-2 accelerometer series behind Figure 3 is not deposited, and Figure 3 cannot be regenerated by any route in the package.
findings.unverifiable_basis: The complete deposited package was searched and all serialized objects were inventoried; only derived summaries were present, so the published figure's underlying series could not be checked or regenerated.

evidence.artifact: pkg/ (all 213 files, including all 27 rds loaded and inventoried)
evidence.operation: search the deposit for the accelerometer series at any granularity
evidence.expected: a per-participant accelerometer series, per the data availability statement
evidence.observed: only the derived per-participant summary is present

findings.remedy_description: Deposit the series, or amend the statement to say which data are available.
benign_explanations_ruled_out: The series could be embedded in an rds: excluded, all 27 rds files were loaded and inventoried.
It could sit in a second deposit: excluded, the article links one OSF component and no other is referenced.

verifiers.notes: Nothing here suggests Figure 3 is wrong; only that it cannot be checked.

findings.claim: The power analysis requires 79 participants; the article states the requirement as 78 and reports an analytic sample of 78.

evidence.operation: recompute the G*Power requirement for 80% power at d = 0.65, two-tailed
evidence.tolerance_note: The computed requirement is 78.4. An integer requirement rounds up: 78.4 participants means 79.

findings.remedy_description: State the requirement as 79 and note that the achieved analytic sample of 78 falls one short of it.
benign_explanations_ruled_out: A different target power or effect size: excluded, both are printed in the article and reproduce 78.4.
A one-tailed test: excluded, the article specifies two-tailed.

verifiers.method: recomputed in G*Power 3.1 from the printed parameters

rollup.overall_rationale: The maximum is set by F3 alone, and its tier travels with it: F3 was established at T3, so the comment's headline finding is a two-day check, not the two-week T4 grind that F4 represents. F5 means the deposit also contains territory we could not enter.
credits: The deposit is self-contained apart from one series and runs from a single master script.
A seed is set and the clustering is reproducible to the digit.
The preregistration is linked from the paper and its primary outcome matches the reported one.

author_response.note: Corresponding author acknowledged within eight days, accepted F1, F2 and F5, and asked for two weeks to check F3 against their own logs. Private correspondence; redact before release.

notes: Coded against SCHEME.md v1.0. The three fields are orthogonal and must never be collapsed: F2 is impact 'none' carrying a real disclosure defect, F6 is a T1 five-minute check that is nonetheless a genuine reporting error, and the comment's impact_max is computed by Rule 1 rather than judged. F5 is 'unverifiable', not 'none' -- the deposit does not support the check, which is an epistemic state and not a clean bill of health.
